name: Continuing education and certification courses
one_line: One professional-development course taken from a provider to earn credit hours toward a credential: the provider's course materials plus the completion certificate that states the credit unit.

deterministic: a credit-unit token (CE, CEU, CPE, CLE, contact-hour or PDU shapes) adjacent to a completion or course term in a high-weight zone — filename, document title, page-one heading, or slide-one title. This is 00's pattern-plus-context shape reused: credits is one of the five academic context terms the design names, and the unit token carries the professional reading the bare word does not
a provider-approval or accreditation statement in a high-weight zone naming an approving body together with a course title on the same page
a Certificate of Completion or Course Completion heading in the title zone together with a named provider and a completion-date slot
a labelled table cell or form field whose label reads Provider, Course, Credits, Credit Hours or Completion Date, on a document already carrying a course title

a gazetteer hit on a professional-provider or accrediting-body list, matched at a word boundary — 00: "It should use word-boundary matching rather than substring matching" — together with a credit-unit token or a course title in the same zone
an ICS SUMMARY or DESCRIPTION field carrying a credit-unit token beside a webinar or course term, where source_type = calendar contributed only as a file-kind signal and never as proof
needs_llm: a provider name that no gazetteer holds and that reads as an ordinary company, where the model must judge from cited text whether the organization is running the course or merely employing the holder
an unlabelled agenda or outline whose only professional-education signal is a contact-hours line in running prose
a certificate or transcript in a language whose credit-unit and completion vocabulary the deterministic pattern catalogue does not cover
an employer training record where the model must decide whether the file is the holder's own coursework or an HR record about other people, and must return unknown when it cannot cite support

a course run by a university's extension or professional-studies arm, where the coursework reading and the continuing-education reading are both supported and 00's rule applies — "conflicting signals should lead to abstention rather than an invented classification"
never_alone: a provider or university name alone — 00: "A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization." Course provider is one of the six ambiguous roles the sentence lists, so the name cannot establish even the provider reading by itself

a certificate-shaped filename or a certificate-shaped layout alone. 00 gives standalone certificates their own residual home precisely because they are common and unattached: "Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group." This is true of the tempting false files below — a platform completion certificate and a licence certificate look identical in the filename

a bare number alone, including a bare credit count and a 4-digit year — 00 warns of "numbers that look like years but are course identifiers, version numbers, build numbers, ZIP codes, or other unrelated values"

a professional licence, registration or membership number alone: it identifies a person and their credential, not a course of study, and it is the evidence that most tempts a false read of a renewal notice as a completed course

a course-code-shaped token with no academic or professional-education context describing the document, which 00's adversarial suite already covers as course-code patterns that are actually other identifiers
source_type or extension alone: a .pdf certificate, an .ics webinar invite, a .xlsx tracker, an .mp4 recording. file_kind is constitutionally never-alone
a parent folder named CE, Training, Certificates or Professional Development alone — folder context is a clue, and 00 requires that existing user structure not be silently reinterpreted
membership in a bounded download session alone — 00: "A session should never be treated as proof of topic"

grouping_reasons: one provider course and everything it produced — the agenda, the handouts, the recording and the completion certificate — anchored by a shared course title, not by a shared provider name alone

one credential's reporting period across several providers, which is purpose-coherent and content-incoherent and therefore needs explicit reporting-period or renewal evidence in the files themselves; a download session or a shared folder is a retrieval clue only
one course across its version family — a certificate reissued after a name correction is the universal version family, not a second course
a sparse handout attached to a course neighbourhood as a context-supported member only — 00: "The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files."

template.why: The schema's recommended order is 00's own — "An Academic template may define school → term → course → work type" — and this situation keeps its shape while dropping term. school comes first because the provider is what makes a prose course title intelligible and disambiguable: two providers routinely sell a course with the same title, which is the same problem 00 describes when it says a course code "may require the school or term to disambiguate it". subject comes before work_type for 00's stated reason: "A work type such as Homework 3 is meaningful only after the course is known". term is dropped rather than demoted because the academic-term rule family cannot fire on material that has no semester, and 00 rejects levels of that kind — a dimension that would "create meaningless one-child levels" or "produce empty branches when tested against the accepted group", where "It should recommend flattening when a dimension does not materially improve retrieval." instructor is excluded because it is not destination-eligible. This is a recommendation the user may reverse, remove or flatten; a professional with few certificates per provider will reasonably flatten to school → work_type, and one who browses by topic will reverse to subject → school.

collides_with.signal: both sides are evidenced by a certificate-shaped PDF naming a person and a professional body. The discriminating evidence: this side needs a named course of study plus a credit-unit statement for that course; the credentials side names the licence, registration or membership itself with an issue or expiry date and no course of study. The renewal-notice and the completion-certificate fixtures above are the two halves of this confusion.

both sides are evidenced by a platform completion certificate carrying a provider, a course title and a completion date. The discriminating evidence: this side needs a credit-unit token or a provider-approval statement from an accrediting body; the online-course side has a platform completion with neither, and its provider value is a platform rather than an approved provider. Neither side may take the certificate layout or the word Certificate alone.

both sides can be evidenced by the word credits, by a course title and by an instructor slot. The discriminating evidence: coursework needs a dedicated academic-term pattern, a course-code-plus-context pair, or enrollment language naming a degree-granting institution; this side needs a credit-unit token in its professional form or an accrediting-body approval line, and characteristically has no term at all. A university extension course clears both, which is an abstention case rather than a silent choice.

both sides can be evidenced by a document titled transcript that lists courses and credits against a person. The discriminating evidence: the transcripts side carries registrar language, a seal or verification code, and grades against a degree programme; this side carries a provider's own credit ledger for professional reporting, with credit units and no grades and no conferred degree.

sensitivity_why: The defining artifact routinely prints the holder's professional licence or registration number beside their legal name, and employer-sponsored training records are employment material. 00 counts both in the corpus it protects: the product "processes a highly personal corpus that can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records." Which handling class applies is P7's and is not set here.
open_question: Two decisions this node cannot make. (1) The dimension a professional actually browses by is the credential the credits are earned toward — CPA, RN, PMP, bar — and no canonical field holds it: it is a career-domain field and career field rows are deferred (D1 as narrowed, PR-6). Until that lands, a credential level cannot be recommended, and the reporting-period grouping reason above has no field to hang on. (2) May term hold a CE reporting or renewal period as a VALUE (a 2025 reporting period, a two-year renewal cycle), or does term stay an academic-semester field, leaving this situation permanently three-dimensional? Reading it as a value would restore a fourth level and would let a period-shaped number reach a field whose validating rule family is explicitly the academic-term pattern; reading it as out of scope is what this node assumed.
